edit.description: the resolved bay root is proven against git's own top-level before any root-derived path is composed, reported as `EX_IOERR` naming both
the refusal over a bay below the top-level, beside the bay-discovery arms

summary: A bay root below git's top-level composes `stateRootRel` in an alphabet git never uses, so every fence glob and queue pathspec silently loses its prefix
acceptance: a resolved bay root that is not the top-level git names paths from refuses at the point of detection, naming both roots, rather than proceeding into a fence and a queue read composed against a root git's own `--name-only` output disagrees with
tests: flume refuses a bay root that is not the git top-level rather than composing paths against it
notes: Field report, 0.19, relocated state root. Reproduced this tick with no FLUME_DIR at all: `<repo>/sub/.flume` as cwd gives `resolveRepoRoot` (`src/cliStateDirs.ts:57`) `<repo>/sub`, `computeStateRootRel` (`src/paths.ts:118`) `.flume`, while git names the same file `sub/.flume/f`. Nothing calls `rev-parse --show-toplevel`. Fork named in the commit body: refuse (here) versus fold `stateRootRel` onto git's top-level, which would keep nested bays working and is the human's to rule.
